features.note: Walled enclosure confirmed in compressor-room.png (closed state) and compressor-room-open.png (wall toggled). The exhaust louver pair is present on the exterior wall: blades fully resolved at native in coupling-exhaust-full crop — two-section frame with horizontal slats, two exhaust fan hubs confirmed as dark circles at distinct positions inside the open louver. Blade state contrast between coupling-exhaust-off (flat/closed bars) and coupling-exhaust-full (edge-on/open grill) is unambiguous. The enclosure reads as a hard boundary — a walled room, not loose equipment. No defect.

Luminaire-grid.png and the hero crop both confirm individual fixtures as cylindrical pendant units with a dark aluminium body and a bright white circular lens — definitively disc-shaped UFO highbays, not emissive boxes. Grid regularity is evident from the pendant positions hanging at uniform truss-bay intervals visible in the hero crop (approximately 15-17 pendant drops counted, consistent with an 18-fixture array partially occluded by the distribution duct). The camera preset frames the ceiling plane and structural grid so the row/column regularity reads. Mild gap: a top-down or further-back camera would allow a confident exact count of all 18; from the current angled-interior preset the count is inferred from regularity rather than enumerated.

AHU box confirmed on the roof structure in ahu-roof.png (dark rectangular unit seated in the truss plane). Riser confirmed as a distinct metallic cylinder descending from the AHU into the bay interior, clearly resolved in duct-run.png where the riser occupies the full left edge of frame and connects directly to the horizontal trunk duct. Trunk duct runs the bay length with green flow-direction markers at diffuser positions. Air path is visibly continuous — riser to duct, no floating segments. The duct-run preset also shows the human scale figure, the compressor-room enclosure box, and a luminaire pendant — spatial context is readable.

Lead and lag compressor cabinets both confirmed in the skid-center crop at native resolution. Each cabinet shows a clearly modeled circular cooling-fan disc with a raised hub ring on its face — not a texture mark. The disc geometry is fully resolved (not a faint circular trace that downscaling could create). The lead cabinet is proportionally larger than the lag, consistent with the spec's 2.0x1.2x1.7m vs 1.9x1.2x1.7m difference. Blue receiver tank with domed top confirmed at native in the receiver-detail crop, distinctly coloured and clearly a vertical cylindrical pressure vessel. Refrigerated dryer reads as a smaller dark rectangular box beside the receiver. Header pipe connecting compressor discharge to receiver is resolved as a thin silver line in the same crop. All four sub-components present. Minor gap: the dark machine-enamel cabinets against the dark interior require native cropping to read clearly; at thumbnail resolution the skid sits in a low-contrast zone.

Column grid confirmed as vertical structural members visible at bay perimeter in multiple captures (compressor-skid.png, duct-run.png). Roof truss structure is prominent in index.png (plan-diagonal view) showing a regular beam grid. Wall cladding is present in index.png and bay-envelope.png, with the bay reading as an enclosed building. The 2:1 plan ratio (40x20m) is legible from the index.png overhead angle. The 8m clear height is contextualised by the scale-reference figure visible in duct-run.png — mechanical equipment occupies the lower 2m of an 8m volume. The bay reads as an industrial facility, not a hollow box.

important_features.note: Header piping from compressor discharge to receiver confirmed in crop-receiver-detail (thin silver pipe at mid-height connecting to receiver side). Distribution main confirmed as the large cylindrical pipe running at high level across the bay interior, visible in compressor-room.png, duct-run.png, and luminaire-grid.png with green flow-direction markers. The route exits the receiver area and traverses the bay longitudinally — sensible routing, no structural penetration issues visible.

Human figure confirmed in luminaire-grid.png (tan/beige biped visible at floor level, centre-foreground) and duct-run.png (same figure at mid-frame, providing clear height context against the 8m clear height and the distribution duct at ~5.5m). The figure reads as approximately 1.8m against the equipment surrounding it.

defects.detail: The machine-enamel compressor cabinets (#54585c) sit against a dark interior in the compressor-skid preset. At display resolution the fan-grille discs are near-invisible and the cabinet form is ambiguous. Native cropping resolves them — the geometry is present — but the feature should be readable without cropping in a gate capture. The ambient fill is insufficient for dark-bodied equipment in a dark room.

The luminaire-grid preset is an angled interior view in which the distribution duct occludes a portion of the fixture array. Approximately 15-17 pendants are countable; 18 is inferred from grid regularity. A top-down or isometric overhead preset would allow enumeration rather than inference. This does not block the feature — the regularity is demonstrably grid-based — but it weakens the evidence chain for an exact-count re-gate.

corrections.action: increase scene ambient or add a fill light inside the compressor room so cabinet faces and fan-grille discs read at display resolution without requiring native cropping
add a top-down or far-back camera preset (e.g. view=luminaire-plan) that frames the full 6x3 array from above so all 18 can be enumerated in a single capture
